items.followUp: Describe the observations in Rutherford’s alpha-particle scattering experiment and explain what they showed about the structure of the atom.

rubric.why: The main apparatus used in the experiment must be identified.
rubric.description: Names the alpha-particle source, gold foil and fluorescent screen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying all three main components.

rubric.why: The labeled arrangement shows how the experiment was set up.
rubric.description: Shows a narrow beam directed at the foil, with a circular screen around the foil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a labeled diagram or equivalent schematic showing the correct arrangement.

rubric.why: These are the key observations made when alpha particles struck the foil.
rubric.description: States that most particles passed straight through, a few were deflected and very few bounced back.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all three observations.

rubric.why: The observations led Rutherford to propose a small, dense, positively charged nucleus in an atom that is mostly empty space.
rubric.description: Gives Rutherford’s conclusion about the atom’s structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms are mostly empty space and contain a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.

modelAnswer: An alpha-particle source in a lead block produced a narrow beam directed at a very thin gold foil.
A circular fluorescent screen coated with zinc sulphide (ZnS) surrounded the foil and showed flashes where alpha particles struck it.
Diagram: [Alpha source in lead block] → [narrow slit] → alpha beam → [thin gold foil]; a circular ZnS fluorescent screen surrounds the foil.
Most alpha particles passed straight through the foil; a few were deflected, and very few bounced back.
Rutherford concluded that atoms are mostly empty space and contain a very small, dense, positively charged nucleus.
